title: Demand Service Rate Programs: Working Out the Labor Line of a Completed Call
content:
## The clause

The labor line for demand work is raised for the call last completed on the rate program, and it is
worked out from the hours the ticket logs for that call, the hours of them the owner is charged for, the
rate those hours are billed at, the premium the band carries and what is billed for any technician
beyond the lead. The hours the ticket logs are taken as they stand, rounded up to the next quarter hour.
Every hour charged for is billed, and none of them is met from prepaid hours. The rate is the tier's
block overage rate, the figure published for the program the account holds under the Demand Service Rate Programs. Hours worked in regular hours carry no premium, the premium those hours carry standing at 1.0.
Nothing further is billed for technicians beyond the lead. The labor line is the hours billed multiplied
by the rate and then by the premium, added to the further technicians' element, which is itself the
number of technicians beyond the lead multiplied by the hours charged for, by the rate that technician
is billed at and by the same premium; the two elements are added and only the total is rounded, to the
nearest cent, half up.

## The clause taken apart

| Quantity | Where it is read from |
|---|---|
| the hours the ticket logs | the completion record of the call last completed on the rate program |
| the hours charged for | those logged hours, rounded up to the next quarter hour |
| the hours billed | the hours charged for, each one of them billed |
| the rate | the block overage rate published for the program the account holds |
| the premium | 1.0, the premium hours worked in regular hours carry |
| the further technicians' element | nothing, nothing further being billed for technicians beyond the lead |

## Worked through on hypothetical hours

A call last completed on a rate program whose published block overage rate is 144 US dollars logs 3.1
technician hours. Rounded up to the next quarter hour the hours charged for are 3.25, and all 3.25 are
billed. Those 3.25 hours multiplied by 144 US dollars give 468 US dollars, and multiplied then by the
premium of 1.0 they stand at 468 US dollars. Nothing further is billed for technicians beyond the lead,
so the further technicians' element is nil, and the total, rounded to the nearest cent, half up, is
468.00 US dollars.

Where the same ticket logged 3.25 hours exactly, the hours charged for would still be 3.25, a quarter
hour needing no rounding up, and the labor line would again be 468.00 US dollars.
